title: The energy of a circular orbit
hook: Change orbital radius and predict orbital-energy magnitude.
misconception: orbital-energy magnitude doubles when orbital radius doubles, regardless of the stated relationship.
objective: Apply energy magnitude = GMm/(2r) to compare orbital-energy magnitude when orbital radius changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With a small orbiting mass in a circular Newtonian orbit around a fixed dominant mass, energy magnitude = GMm/(2r). When orbital radius doubles, orbital-energy magnitude becomes ½ times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model energy magnitude = GMm/(2r); scaling exponent -1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider a small orbiting mass in a circular Newtonian orbit around a fixed dominant mass, with a nonzero initial result. If orbital radius triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on orbital-energy magnitude?
recall.why: Apply energy magnitude = GMm/(2r) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 1/3.
